propositions: Inbound link removal never converges when an ordered pair holds two differently-related net-active dependencies (e.g. blocks and relates_to simultaneously) because removal is pair-scoped but write is relation-scoped

Guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one permanently declines removal when the pair's most-recent net-active relation differs from the vanished relation's relation, causing the remove record to re-emit and re-decline every reconcile pass

Direction-agnostic deduping on (vendor_type, target_key) in outbound differs causes outbound ADD to be suppressed when a same-vendor-type remote link exists, allowing inbound remove records to survive past G4 suppression and reach G5
Relation-scoped removal seam keyed on (target_id, relation) is required to make removal symmetric with writes and enable inbound unlink convergence for double-related pairs
CLI rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation] must support optional relation argument to remain backward-compatible with pair-scoped most-recent behavior when relation is omitted
Removal of a named relation with no matching net-active local link must be a logged no-op, never removing other relations or links the peer still carries
